question: A veterinarian presents with chronic low-grade fever, night sweats, joint pain and hepatosplenomegaly. He works with cattle and goats and regularly drinks unpasteurised milk. Which investigation combination will BEST confirm the suspected diagnosis?

answers.text: Blood culture in Castaneda biphasic medium + standard agglutination test (SAT) with 2-mercaptoethanol

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Brucellosis is strongly suggested by chronic undulating fever, arthralgia, hepatosplenomegaly and occupational livestock/dairy exposure. Castaneda biphasic medium allows isolation with prolonged incubation (≥21 days). SAT titre ≥1:160 is significant; 2-ME treatment eliminates IgM, confirming active IgG-mediated chronic disease.

answers.text: Widal test + blood culture in bile broth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Widal test and bile broth culture are used for enteric fever (Salmonella typhi). The chronic course with arthralgia, hepatosplenomegaly and occupational livestock contact points to brucellosis, not typhoid fever.

answers.text: MAT (microscopic agglutination test) + culture in EMJH medium

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MAT and EMJH culture are specific for leptospirosis. While leptospirosis causes fever with organ dysfunction, its acute presentation with monsoon or flood exposure differs from this chronic occupational syndrome with arthralgia.

While extrapulmonary tuberculosis can cause chronic fever and hepatosplenomegaly, the specific combination of livestock contact, unpasteurised dairy consumption, undulating fever and arthralgia is characteristic of brucellosis, not TB.

overallFeedback.feedback: Apply the investigation framework: Step 1 — epidemiological clue (livestock contact, unpasteurised dairy); Step 2 — syndrome recognition (chronic undulating fever, arthralgia, hepatosplenomegaly) → brucellosis; Step 3 — select Castaneda biphasic culture + SAT with 2-ME.

Well done! You correctly matched the epidemiological clue (livestock, unpasteurised dairy) and clinical syndrome (chronic undulating fever, arthralgia, hepatosplenomegaly) to brucellosis and its specific diagnostic tests.
